text.en: Toys, tents, capsules and ice-cream cones are made by joining solids. To find their cost or capacity we split them into basic solids.

A combined solid is formed by joining two or more basic solids such as cylinder, cone, hemisphere and cuboid.
For surface area, count only the surfaces visible from outside; joined faces are not counted.
For volume, add the volumes of the parts.
A cylinder surmounted by a hemisphere has total surface area pi r (2h plus 3r), where h is the cylinder height only.
A tent made of a cylinder surmounted by a cone has volume pi r squared (h1 plus h2 over 3).
For a funnel, the outer surface is the curved surface of the cylinder plus the curved surface of the frustum.
When a hemisphere is cut out of a cube, the new surface area is 6 times the edge squared plus pi r squared.

problem.en: A toy is a cylinder surmounted by a hemisphere. Total height 25 cm and common diameter 12 cm. Find the total surface area.

text.en: Radius r = 6 cm. Height of the cylinder h = 25 - 6 = 19 cm.

why.en: The hemisphere takes 6 cm of the height.

text.en: TSA = CSA of cylinder + CSA of hemisphere + base of cylinder = 2 pi r h + 2 pi r^2 + pi r^2.

prompt.en: A tent for 150 people: each needs 4 sq. m of floor and 40 cu. m of air. The cylindrical part is 8 m high. Find the height of the cone.

requiredIdeas.en: Base area = 150 x 4 = 600 sq. m so pi r^2 = 600
h2/3 = 2 so the cone height is 6 m

commonMisconceptions.en: Treating the tent as only a cylinder

points.en: Read heights carefully: total versus part.
